_note: SL-007 O-046 / RD-m1, closed as its class: rights a freshly created file is granted by its creating open but which the write's later open of that file is checked for. Windows checks the folder's rights for a CREATE (FILE_ADD_FILE) and then hands the creating handle whatever access it asked for, whatever the folder's inherited rights on files say. The write's move, a later open of its temporary for DELETE, is checked. So a probe that only creates can say a folder is writable when the move will be refused. Members come from whoever sets a folder's rights, by design and not to get past anything: a drop or inbox folder that takes files and lets no one remove them, a share with delete withheld, a read-only mirror. 'rules' are Deny entries for the current account on the folder: 'applies' is 'folder' (the folder itself) or 'files' (inherited by the files made in it); 'rights' is a System.Security.AccessControl.FileSystemRights name. 'probe' and 'write' say what ReportFile.Probe and then ReportFile.Write do in that folder: 'ok' or 'refused' (IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException, which the app maps to exit 3). ReportFileFolderRightsCorpusTests runs every row and also holds the property of the whole class: the probe is refused exactly when the write is. 'before' says what the probe did before it deleted its own file while holding the handle: where it differs from the write, that was the defect.
